narrative: Your law school application was denied because the predictive model estimated a 73% chance you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. This high probability of failure was the basis for rejecting your admission. The model’s decision was driven most strongly by your class rank in your third year, followed by your rank in your first year, and then your undergraduate GPA. Specifically, your third-year rank placed you in the lowest decile (1 out of 10), while accepted students average around the 6th decile; this was the single largest factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Your first-year rank was also in the lowest decile, again well below the accepted average, and it was the second most influential factor, also pushing toward failure. In contrast, your undergraduate GPA of 3.20, though slightly below the accepted average of 3.23, was the third most important feature and actually pushed the prediction toward passing. To improve your chances in a future application, focus on strengthening your academic record—especially raising your class standing in advanced law courses—and consider retaking the LSAT (your score of 31 is below the accepted average of 37.18). Seek academic advising and consider gaining relevant work experience before reapplying.
